one_liner: CRM for deal, pipeline, and relationship intelligence management.
blocker: API credentials require an existing DealCloud customer site where an org admin enables the 'API' capability for the user's group; no self-serve developer signup or free tier is documented.

evidence.claim: Authentication uses OAuth2 client credentials to obtain a bearer token
evidence.quote: DealCloud uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow to generate a bearer token, which is then used in the HTTP Authentication header for API requests.

evidence.claim: API access must be enabled by a workspace admin via user-group permissions
evidence.quote: To enable API access, ensure the intended user is assigned to a user group with the appropriate permissions. Navigate to Admin > User Management

evidence.claim: Once permitted, users self-serve an API key from their profile
evidence.quote: Scroll down to the API Key section and click Enable. Then click Copy API Key to Clipboard to copy your API key for use in integrations or API requests.

evidence.claim: The public API surface is REST with multiple functional areas and endpoints
evidence.quote: Our APIs are organized into functional areas. Each area includes multiple endpoints designed to help you perform specific tasks related to that category.

evidence.claim: An official vendor MCP server exists with read-only tools
evidence.quote: All DealCloud MCP tools are currently read-only and do not create, update, or delete data.

notes: Official DealCloud MCP Server documented, in client preview starting July 2026; MCP auth is a per-user OAuth sign-in flow and tools include GraphQL execute_query/introspect/search_schema. Python SDK (dealcloud_sdk) supports env, JSON, and YAML credential loading. Bearer tokens expire after 900 seconds and must be re-requested. Scopes gate API areas (data, user_management, publish, ri_import, backup). Schema APIs limited to 5 calls/second. Docs assume an existing enterprise DealCloud site; no public signup or free developer tier is mentioned.
